title: Symplectic integration with SIMP

code: grad_U <- function(q) q out <- simp_integrate(   q0 = c(1, 0), p0 = c(0, 1), grad_U = grad_U,   eps = 0.1, n_steps = 200, integrator = "leapfrog", trajectory = TRUE)  plot(out$q_path[, 1], out$p_path[, 1], type = "l", asp = 1,      xlab = "q", ylab = "p", main = "Leapfrog trajectory")

title: Symplectic integration with SIMP
text: Pass U record total energy along path. symplectic integrator keeps bounded band. two-stage minerror2 cancels leading error term Gaussian target, energy error sits far leapfrog’s step size, two gradient evaluations per step.
code: U <- function(q) 0.5 * sum(q^2) energy_err <- function(scheme) {   o <- simp_integrate(c(1, 0), c(0, 1), grad_U, eps = 0.3, n_steps = 200,                       integrator = scheme, trajectory = TRUE, U = U)   pmax(abs(o$energy - o$energy[1]), .Machine$double.eps) } schemes <- c("leapfrog", "minerror2", "yoshida4") errs <- lapply(schemes, energy_err)  matplot(seq_len(201), do.call(cbind, errs), type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2,         log = "y", xlab = "step", ylab = "|H(t) - H(0)|",         main = "Energy error by integrator") legend("topright", legend = schemes, col = seq_along(schemes), lty = 1, lwd = 2)

title: Symplectic integration with SIMP
text: simp_hmc() draws proposal integrating target’s Hamiltonian flow accepting Metropolis rule energy. integrator free choice, scheme can drive sampler.
code: Sigma <- matrix(c(1, 0.8, 0.8, 1), 2) P <- solve(Sigma) U_hmc <- function(q) 0.5 * as.numeric(t(q) %*% P %*% q) grad_hmc <- function(q) as.numeric(P %*% q)  fit <- simp_hmc(U_hmc, grad_hmc, init = c(0, 0), n_iter = 2000, eps = 0.25,                 n_steps = 16, warmup = 500, integrator = "minerror2")  colMeans(fit$draws)      # target mean is c(0, 0) #> [1] -0.0005825939 -0.0005670790 cov(fit$draws)           # target covariance is Sigma #>           [,1]      [,2] #> [1,] 0.6909171 0.4657506 #> [2,] 0.4657506 0.6618505 fit$accept_rate #> [1] 1

title: Symplectic integration with SIMP
text: kinetic potential parts separate, Riemannian dynamics position-dependent mass m(q), explicit schemes longer apply. simp_integrate_nonsep() uses generalized (implicit) leapfrog, solves two implicit stages fixed-point iteration. m(q) = 1 + 0.5 q^2. separable Hamiltonian generalized leapfrog reduces standard leapfrog, strict extension explicit path.
code: m  <- function(q) 1 + 0.5 * q^2 H  <- function(q, p) 0.5 * p^2 / m(q) + 0.5 * q^2 dHdq <- function(q, p) -0.5 * p^2 * q / m(q)^2 + q dHdp <- function(q, p) p / m(q)  ns <- simp_integrate_nonsep(   q0 = 1, p0 = 0.5, dH_dq = dHdq, dH_dp = dHdp,   eps = 0.05, n_steps = 400, trajectory = TRUE, H = H)  ns$converged #> [1] TRUE range(ns$energy)  # bounded: energy is conserved #> [1] 0.5831680 0.5833571

Exposed C++ simp::two_stage_adaptive / simp::three_stage_adaptive <simp/adapt.h>. Exact harmonic energy-error analysis backing adaptation, <simp/harmonic.h>: simp::harmonic_energy_error(scheme, nu) relative energy-oscillation amplitude scheme induces unit oscillator dimensionless step nu, simp::harmonic_stability_limit(scheme) largest stable step. come scheme’s exact 2x2 propagation matrix invariant quadratic form. Parametric multistage constructors simp::two_stage(b) simp::three_stage(b, ) <simp/scheme.h>; minerror2() now b = (3 - sqrt(5)) / 4 member two_stage. simp_integrate_mts() advances split potential U = U_slow + U_fast multiple-time-stepping (RESPA / Verlet-) integrator: slow force evaluated per outer step fast force drives m inner substeps, stiff--cheap part takes small steps without expensive part paying rate. Exposed C++ simp::step_mts / simp::integrate_mts <simp/mts.h>.

Recovery tests cover new members: minerror2 energy cancellation order nonlinear problem, generalized leapfrog’s separable-reduction, energy conservation, reversibility.
